MINUTES
  MALIBU PLANNING COMMISSION
  REGULAR MEETING
  MAY 2, 2022
  TELECONFERENCED VARIOUS LOCATIONS
  -

  6:30 P.M.

The following meeting was held pursuant to the Governor’s Executive Orders N~25-20
and N-29-20 and fully teleconferenced from various locations during the coronavirus
disease (COVID-19) pandemic.

CALL TO ORDER

  Chair Hill called the meeting to order at 6:31 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Chair Kraig Hill, Vice Chair Dennis Robert Smith, and Commissioners
  Jeffrey Jennings, John Mazza, and Mark Wetton

  ALSO PRESENT: Richard Mollica, Planning Director; Trevor Rusin, Assistant City
  Attorney; Troy Spayd, Assistant Public Works Director; Courtney McCammon, City
  Biologist; Tyler Eaton, Associate Planner; Raneika Brooks, Senior Planner; Lauren
  Doyel, Coastal Engineer and Geotechnical Reviewer; and Rebecca Evans, Recording
  Secretary

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Commissioner Mazza moved and Commissioner Jennings seconded a motion to
  approve the agenda as recommended by staff.

  The question was called and the motion carried unanimously.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  Recording Secretary Evans reported that the agenda for the meeting was properly posted
  on April 22, 2022.

ITEM 1  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS
  None.

ITEM 2.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS
   Malibu Planning Commission
  Minutes of May 2, 2022
  Page 2 of 8

  Alex Stein made a request for the Commissioners to block access to a residential
  street.

  Terry Winders ceded his time and chose not to provide public comment.

ITEM 2.B.  COMMISSION / STAFF COMMENTS

  Commissioner Jennings suggested when meetings return to City Hall, a hybrid
  format be considered to allow applicants and staff to join remotely to save the
  City and applicants time and money.

  Commissioner Mazza asked for clarification on live versus virtual meetings
  currently scheduled. He stated that a hybrid format would be preferable in the
  future.

  Commissioner Wetton concurred that applicant teams and staff should continue to
  be able to present via Zoom.

  Chair Hill noted that the City Clerk may be able to set up a hybrid format within a
  month or two should the City Council choose to revisit its decision.

  Planning Director Mollica stated the May 9, 2022 City Council and the May 16,
  2022 Planning Commission meetings will take place in Council Chambers. He
  added that meetings which followed those dates would take place via Zoom and
  there would be no call ins for the in-person meeting.

  Chair Hill asked if call-ins to a live meeting could be restricted to a limited group
  such as residents. He also asked for clarification on why the Special Planning
  Commission was scheduled for May 31, 2022 on a day when he was unable to
  attend.

  Assistant City Attorney Rusin stated that it would be illegal to limit call-ins to a
  subset of the population.

  Planning Director Mollica explained that Planning staff have been trying to work
  with the school district. However, the District’s time schedule was highly
  aggressive due to rising construction costs and dates when students were present
  on campus. He added the school district asked for a June 13, 2022 meeting of the
  City Council, which must be preceded with a twenty-one-day notice. He
  explained that should the Planning Commission be scheduled any later, the City
  Council report would be written prior to the Planning Commission hearing the
  matter. He further explained that if this body were to ask for more time, it would
  cause further project delay.
   Malibu Planning Commission
  Minutes of May 2, 2022
  Page 3 of 8

  Commissioner Jennings asked if Code Enforcement was aware that the school
  district recently placed ten to twenty K-rails, concrete barriers, along Merritt
  Drive. He explained that the workers who dropped off the material stated they did
  not have a City permit but received direction from the school district and the K-
  rails appeared to be blocking part of the public right-of-way.

  In response to Commissioner Jennings, Planning Director Mollica stated Code
  Enforcement had reached out to the District. The District stated that there used to
  be dirt berms in that location that prevented vehicles from driving onto school
  property. He explained that Code Enforcement staff requested the District to
  formally submit to the City.

  Vice Chair Smith asked for the City to consider adding an afternoon session such
  as 2:00 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. at least one day per week to supplement the City
  Biologist morning counter hours. The City Biologist had very limited availability
  and should be at City Hall at least four hours or preferably two days per week
  rather than one. He noted that some members of the public imposed excessive
  demands on staff time through numerous requests and expressed hope that City
  Manager McClary would impose limits to allow staff time to be spent on projects.
  He stated his preference for a return to in-person meetings.

  Planning Director Mollica calendared a meeting to discuss the City Biologist’s
  schedule, balanced between time in City Hall and final site visits for fire rebuilds.

  Planning Director Mollica informed the Commission that a synopsis memo
  regarding the wireless tower re-installed at the College site was available on the
  City’s website. He further elaborated on the details of the wireless tower.

  Commissioner Mazza stated the Commission approved a tension tower with bars
  rather than a smokestack and the former tower had no railings, which exist in the
  rebuilt tower. He asked why the Federal Aviation Administration wanted a
  mandate on a tower below the roofline.

  Chair Hill agreed the prior tower was view permeable unlike the present
  construction.

ITEM 3  CONSENT CALENDAR

MOTION  Commissioner Mazza moved and Commissioner Jennings seconded a motion to
  approve the Consent Calendar. The question was called and the motion carried
  unanimously.
   Malibu Planning Commission
  Minutes of May 2, 2022

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following items:

  A.  Previously Discussed Items
  None.

  B.  New Items

  extend the Planning Commission’s approval of an application for the

  Location:  31438 Broad Beach Road, within the appealable coastal

  APN:  4470-017-065
  Owner:  2XMD Partners, LLC
  Case Planner: Associate Planner Eaton, 456-2489, ext. 273
  Recommended Action: Adopt Planning Commission Resolution No. 22-

  protection of_an existing slope and surrounding properties located in the
  Single-Family Medium Density_zoning district at 31438 Broad Beach

  Owner:  Issac Real Estate Holdings, Series LLC, Series A

  Case Planner: Assistant Planning Director Fernandez, 456-2489, ext. 482
  Recommended Action: Adopt Planning Commission Resolution No. 22-34

  two-unit duplex into a two-unit condominium, and addition, partial demolition,

  system for the unit located at 20550 Pacific Coast Highway, including Conditional

  Planning Director Mol I ica presented the staff report.

  Speakers: Kristina Kropp, Nick Barsocchini, Greg Torres, John Deirmenjian and

  and installation of a replacement onsite wastewater treatment system for the unit

  located at 20550 Pacific Coast Highway, including Conditional Use Permit No.
  18-006 for the existing multi-family use, and Variance No. 18-043 for the
  conversion of a required unenclosed parking space into an enclosed parking space
  not in compliance with the minimum width requirement in the Multi-Family,
  Beachfront zoning district located at 20550 Pacific Coast Highway (CJAH
  Properties, LLC and Sugerman)

  The Commission discussed the motion and directed questions to staff.

  The question was called and the motion carried 3-2, Commissioner Jennings and

RECESS  The meeting was recessed at 8:03  p.m.  and resumed at 8:10 p.m. with all
  Commissioners present.

  B.  Coastal Development Permit No. 19-064 and Minor Modification No. 2 1-003 An  —

  application for a new single-family residence and associated development
  (Continued from February 7, 2022)
  Location:  28116 Pacific Coast Highway, within the appealable coastal zone
  APN:  4460-033-012
  Owner:  Lot 21, LLC
  Case Planner: Senior Planner Brooks, 456-2489, ext. 276
  Recommended Action: Adopt Planning Commission Resolution No. 22-07
  determining the project is categorically exempt from the California Environmental
  Quality Act, and approving Coastal Development Permit No. 19-064 for the
  construction of a new 1,192 square foot, one-story single-family residence plus a
  484 square foot basement, a I ,32 I square foot detached garage and storage area
  plus a I ,457 square foot basement, fencing, gates, landscaping, hardscape, grading,
  retaining walls, and onsite wastewater treatment system; including Minor
  Modification No. 21-003 to reduce the front yard setback by no more than 50
  percent to allow a solid vehicle entry gate with a height up to 6 feet, 8 inches,
  located in the Rural Residential-Two Acres zoning district at 28116 Pacific Coast
  Highway (Lot 21, LLC)

  Senior Planner Brooks presented the staff report.

  City Biologist McCammon, Assistant Public Works Director Spayd and Coastal
  Engineer and Geotechnical Reviewer Doyel were available for questions.

  Disclosures: Commissioners Mazza, Wetton, Smith and Hill

  The Commission directed questions to staff.
   Malibu Planning Commission
  Minutes of May 2, 2022
  Page 7 of 8

  As there were no further questions for staff, Chair Hill opened the public hearing.

  Speakers: Jairne Harnish, Dan Yoder, Justin Block, Steven Dernsher from the
  applicant team were available to respond to questions

  As there were no other speakers present, Chair Hill closed the public comment
  portion of the public hearing and returned the matter to the table for discussion.

MOTION  Commissioner Mazza moved and Chair Hill seconded a motion to adopt Planning
  Commission Resolution No. 22-07 as amended 1) removing Condition 90; 2)
  removing Condition 93; 3) adding a condition of approval stating, “A Covenant of
  Easement pursuant to MMC Section 17.49 shall be included in a form and manner
  approved by the City Attorney to provide ingress and egress to the properties
  located at 28126 and 28118 PCH as required by CDP 11-033 and APR 18-009”; 4)
  adding a Condition to state “A qualified archaeologist must be present at the site to
  monitor all site excavation. Prior to the issuance of any development permit, the
  property owners or applicant must provide evidence that an archaeologist has been
  contracted to perform the required monitoring. After the monitoring is concluded,
  the qualified archaeologist is required to provide a summary in writing describing
  the monitoring findings;” and 5) determining the project is categorically exempt
  from the California Environmental Quality Act, and approving Coastal
  Development Permit No. 19-064 for the construction of a new 1,192 square foot,
  one-story single-family residence plus a 484 square foot basement, a 1,321 square
  foot detached garage and storage area plus a 1,457 square foot basement, fencing,
  gates, landscaping, hardscape, grading, retaining walls, and onsite wastewater
  treatment system; including Minor Modification No. 21-003 to reduce the front
  yard setback by no more than 50 percent to allow a solid vehicle entry gate with a
  height up to 6 feet, 8 inches, located in the Rural Residential-Two Acres zoning
  district at 28116 Pacific Coast Highway (Lot 21, LLC)

  The Commission discussed the motion and directed questions to staff.

  The question was called and the motion carried 4-1, Vice Chair Smith dissenting.
